Documentation / Developer / Document typography and font licensing

Document typography and font licensing

Perastage resolves the requested family, weight and style to the exact approved font bytes before composition. FontCatalog owns immutable resource data, version, PostScript face name, OFL provenance and SHA-256. Rendering targets use the resolved fingerprint and glyph ID. Persisted styles keep the family and variant authored by the user, so substituting a face does not change the project.

Approved resources

PerastageSans is the application name for the original Noto Sans face. It is the default family. PerastageSans, Noto Serif and Source Sans 3 offer Regular, Bold, Italic and Bold Italic. Noto Sans Mono offers Regular and Bold. Noto Sans Arabic and Noto Sans Hebrew supply upright Regular and Bold script fallback. Third-party notices identify the exact releases, files and licenses. Only these SHA-256 identities enter the catalog. The files are static single-face TrueType fonts with unrestricted embedding flags. An unrestricted OS/2.fsType on its own gives no license evidence.

The packaged catalog checks its pinned files at application initialization. The existing targeted probes and bounded file walk can recover a missing portable face only when its fingerprint matches a bundled approval record.

Installed fonts

DirectWrite on Windows, CoreText on macOS and Fontconfig on Linux enumerate registered font metadata. Windows uses DirectWrite's local file provider. macOS resolves the CoreText PostScript name against a file's faces. Linux uses Fontconfig's index. Remote, private or provider-only faces without a readable file are outside this scope. Enumeration records family, style and file identity and stats each distinct file once. The first selection validates the face in FreeType and hashes the selected bytes. Ordinary installed faces are independent of the bundled allowlist. No system font is redistributed with the application or written to PSTG, MVR, GDTF or a Layout template.

The catalog holds immutable discovery data and bounded loaded-face caches. Resolution and PDF registries keep shared ownership of any resources they use. Glyphs carry owned fingerprint strings. FreeType outlines and HarfBuzz shaping use the same file bytes and collection index. The cache rejects an unloaded face if its file changed after discovery. Refresh publishes a new snapshot, allowing open project references and render caches to resolve against the updated font collection. An explicit Linux refresh forces Fontconfig to rebuild its registered directory caches even when directory timestamps have not changed. Startup uses the normal operating-system caches.

System font references keep the authored family and the per-style PostScript names and fingerprints when available. Layout rich text records these references in run properties. Resolution tries the exact identity, a compatible named or same-family face, and the bundled style and script fallbacks. Files, collection indices and system registration paths are local details. Unavailable requested styles use real faces and never synthesize weight or slant.

Installed font capability Local display PDF
Static standalone TrueType with installable or editable embedding Yes Full program
No subsetting Yes Full program when other flags permit
Preview-and-print only Yes Portable fallback. The writer does not enforce read-only access.
Restricted, bitmap-only or ambiguous rights Yes for supported outlines Portable fallback
Static OpenType/CFF and compatible TrueType or CFF collection faces Yes Portable fallback
Variable instances, color fonts, non-scalable bitmap fonts and web containers Unsupported Portable fallback

Embedding rights follow the OpenType OS/2 specification. OS/2 versions 0 and 1 ignore the unassigned high bits. Versions 0 through 2 allow the least-restrictive permission among conflicting permission bits. Modern conflicting permission bits are invalid. Font metadata does not establish redistribution rights or override the applicable license.

Composition and adapters

HarfBuzz applies OpenType shaping, kerning, positioning and ligatures. ICU computes grapheme boundaries, line opportunities and visual bidi runs, with paragraph embedding levels retained across wrapping. The renderer receives stable face fingerprints, glyph IDs, UTF-8 cluster ranges, positions, offsets, advances and baselines in scene metres or document points. Font selection checks whole graphemes before shaping and groups adjacent graphemes with the same face, direction, script and style. Unicode source is preserved as authored. HarfBuzz handles canonical equivalents such as precomposed and decomposed accents during shaping. FreeType reads the validated font bytes for simple, composite and transformed contours, including quadratic and cubic curves. A malformed outline uses the approved face's missing-glyph contour and records a diagnostic.

The approved repertoire covers Western European text, Greek, Cyrillic, Arabic and Hebrew where the selected or fallback face supplies the required glyphs. Full CJK and emoji coverage are outside the bundled repertoire. Unsupported clusters retain their source and use a missing-glyph contour where available. Script fallback uses real upright Arabic and Hebrew faces even when the surrounding text requests italic.

Fixture Label Editor drafts, source 2D labels and Layout capture share their existing field composition. The default face preserves the established NanoVG halo and the shared positions. Other approved faces use their glyph contours. Layout replay renders the captured contours with the stored physical outline widths. Raster antialiasing and the zoom-independent 2D halo policy may differ from paper ink. Generic Canvas commands resolve through the same catalog in Layout replay and PDF. They accept the approved family name, an optional face suffix such as Bold Italic, and the historic sans and perastage-sans aliases with their bold variants.

Free text uses the same point-space text block plan for Layout and PDF. Rich text remains serialized in its original wx XML model. Extraction preserves families, weights, sizes, italic requests, foreground colors, underlines, strikethrough, explicit breaks, paragraph alignment, spacing and indentation. Edited content stores its wrapping behavior explicitly. Legacy definitions without that setting use the recorded compatibility defaults, independent of which fonts are installed or missing. New content records wrapping explicitly. Legacy native-font metrics could vary by platform. Default sizing now uses the shipped faces, so historical free-text widths can change. Non-text rich objects and uncommon XML style features remain in the source XML with limited rendering support. The Document preview button renders the current edits with the shared point-space composition. The native editor registers approved faces where wxWidgets supports it. Native rendering and caret geometry can vary by platform. Opening and accepting the dialog without editing text keeps the original rich-text XML byte for byte. When wxWidgets cannot round-trip some of the source, the editor displays a notice and keeps the original UTF-8 XML as a Base64 recovery comment beside the edited XML. Subsequent edits keep the same recovery copy. Rendering and export use the active, editable XML.

Legend and Event Table retain their shared point-space composition and size formulas from the integration branch. The older split-export PDF compensation had already been replaced there. Fixture names retain their historical two-space-delimited-word breaks. Viewport capture and Layout raster archives invalidate incompatible plans. The existing per-viewport label cache and bounded shared outline cache avoid repeating glyph work.

PDF output and persistence

The exporter uses Type 0 fonts with TrueType CIDFont descendants, an explicit CID-to-glyph map and a ToUnicode CMap. CIDs encode glyph IDs and the original UTF-16 sequence, including surrogate pairs and ligature source. A multi-glyph cluster uses a PDF ActualText span around its selectable glyphs. Adjacent left-to-right glyphs can share a span with a source space so readers preserve the space during extraction. The PDF places glyphs at the composed positions. It draws fixture outlines as vector paths and leaves the glyph fill selectable. Only used embeddable faces are written. Before placing PDF glyphs, a restricted or unsupported face is resolved to a portable face and the logical text is recomposed. Fixture capture stores the original field text and the anchor needed for that recomposition. The PDF registry also rejects disallowed resources at the point where glyphs and outlines are emitted. Missing faces and unsupported glyphs are recorded once per issue in the export report. Font resource failure leaves scene contents and requested style values intact.

Label presentation version 3 added the optional fontFamily field. Version 4 adds italic where requested. Layout reads all three versions starting at 2. Unchanged legacy label styles continue to write version 2. Legends and Event Tables have an optional fontFamily property in the existing Layout schema and use the default when the field is absent. Free text retains its existing per-run rich-text data. PSTG and templates store presentation choices without introducing font data into MVR or GDTF. Reopening a project revalidates an incomplete catalog, allowing restored packaged or installed resources to recover the requested appearance. The Layout text editor's Refresh fonts action also rechecks a complete catalog. Resource fingerprints invalidate the relevant capture and composition caches.

Verification

PdfFontMetricsEncoding covers catalog authorization, exact installed-face recovery, actual glyph identity, fallback, advances and mixed-family runs. LayoutLicensedFontsPdf uses Poppler to validate a representative Layout's faces, logical Unicode extraction in the default mode, and outline/selection behavior. The PDF fixture uses the production fixture label compositor for Arabic, Hebrew, ligatures and combining marks. The native smoke test exercises editor and viewport capture of a fixture with mixed-direction text. Raw mode also checks text and spaces. Depending on the Poppler release it may emit RTL glyphs in PDF drawing order. Official Windows, Linux and macOS CI require Poppler. A local configuration without Poppler reports the missing validation tools and still runs the structural test. Layout preview and PDF tests compare geometry in document points. The raster parity tests compare ink geometry with tolerances for antialiasing and rasterizer differences.

HarfBuzz, FreeType and ICU are required CMake dependencies and are resolved from the pinned vcpkg manifest for official builds. ICU supplies Unicode segmentation and bidi through its C API. See the third-party notices for their licenses and transitive package notices.
